description: Exploration: FSS, DSS, route plotting, system scanning

entries.content: The Full Spectrum Scanner (FSS) resolves all bodies in a system from any point within the system and is the primary discovery tool. The Detailed Surface Scanner (DSS) must be used at close range to a specific body to map its surface, reveal geological and biological signals, and earn the mapping bonus on the exploration data.
entries._justification: Phase 1 seed entry. No changes needed.

entries.content: The Loadout journal event provides MaxJumpRange in light-years. Frontier documents it as based on zero cargo and just enough fuel for one jump. OmniCOVAS reads jump_range_ly directly from this field and does NOT recompute it from first principles. First-principles jump range calculation requires independently verified FSD constants and mass inputs.
entries.source: Elite Dangerous journal documentation, Loadout event schema
entries._justification: Week 7. Documents the intentional architecture decision: Phase 2 reads Loadout.MaxJumpRange, not physics. Prevents accidental first-principles reimplementation in Pillar 1.

entries.topic: Typical Jump Range Values by Ship Class
entries.content: Jump ranges vary significantly by ship class and FSD engineering. Typical unengineered values: Sidewinder ~7-10 ly, Eagle ~14 ly, Cobra Mk III ~20-25 ly, Python ~8-15 ly (heavy cargo ship), Anaconda ~9-22 ly, Asp Explorer ~25-35 ly. Engineered FSDs (Increased Range, Long Range mod) can add 50-100% to base range. These are reference values only; actual range comes from Loadout.MaxJumpRange.
entries.source: community ship guides, EDDB ship data, in-game testing
entries._justification: Week 7. Reference for sanity-checking jump_range_ly values in tests and debugging. Medium confidence because these are approximate community values, not Frontier-published specs. Needs review against current game version.

entries.topic: Exploration Scan Value by Body Class (reference, community-derived)
entries.content: Exploration payouts vary by orders of magnitude with body class, and are further modified by terraform state, whether the Commander was the first to discover the body, and whether it was surface-mapped with a Detailed Surface Scanner. Approximate base ranges, before bonuses: icy and rocky bodies are negligible, in the hundreds of credits; gas giants of most classes are low, roughly one to five thousand; high metal content bodies are moderate, roughly nine to fifteen thousand; metal-rich bodies roughly twenty to thirty thousand; ammonia worlds and water worlds are high, roughly ninety thousand to one hundred and twenty thousand; Earth-like worlds are very high, in the region of a quarter of a million. Stars are generally low, one to three thousand, except neutron stars and black holes which are roughly twenty thousand. Terraformable candidates carry a substantial premium over their non-terraformable equivalents. First discovery and surface mapping each multiply the figure significantly, and mapping a body the Commander also discovered first pays the most. These are approximate community-derived bands for expectation-setting only. They are NOT Frontier-published, they change with balance patches, and the exact per-body figure depends on mass and other terms this reference deliberately does not model. Actual credits received are reported by the journal in SellExplorationData and MultiSellExplorationData and must always take precedence.
entries.source: community value tables and in-game observation; not Frontier-published
entries._justification: Phase 13 exploration value slice. Entered as class bands rather than a formula on purpose: the real payout depends on mass and other terms, so a precise figure would be confidently wrong. Consumers must present a value CLASS and range, never a single credit number, and must never add the estimate to observed earnings.

entries.content: Flying through the jet cone of a neutron star applies a 4x FSD boost for the next hyperspace jump, allowing significantly longer single jumps than the ship's base MaxJumpRange. This boosted jump range is NOT reflected in Loadout.MaxJumpRange -- the boost is temporary and applied at jump time. Phase 2 does not model neutron boosts; this is Exploration pillar (Phase 5) territory.
entries._justification: Week 7. Documents a known gap in Phase 2 jump range tracking. Neutron boosts appear as anomalously long jumps in FSDJump event data -- Phase 5 will handle these.
